description: Final taxonomically harmonised species name from a taxonomic backbone such as WCVP or GBIF.
Family name as the GBIF backbone accepts it. Given beside wcvp_family because the two backbones place some families differently and neither is silently preferred.
Genus name as the GBIF backbone accepts it.
Plant order from the GBIF backbone, filled for 99.7% of matched names. This is the order to group or filter on.
Species name as the GBIF backbone accepts it.
How the source name met the GBIF backbone: the match status GBIF returned, such as accepted or synonym.
GBIF backbone usage key for the matched name, for linking out to GBIF.
Original species name reported by the primary source, when available.
Species name or accepted/source-resolved name supplied by the downloaded secondary dataset, when available.
Plant family name reported by the source or added during taxonomy matching.
Plant genus name reported by the source or added during taxonomy matching.
Plant order name as the source reported it. Filled for about a third of records and the sources disagree with each other, so it is provenance only - group and filter on gbif_order instead.
Family name as WCVP accepts it.
Genus name as WCVP accepts it.
Species name as WCVP (World Checklist of Vascular Plants) accepts it.
How the source name met WCVP: an exact match, a match to a synonym resolved to the accepted name, or a fuzzy match.
Primary reference, citation, DOI, or source-reference field reported in the dataset.
Folder/source identifier for the downloaded dataset.
File within the source folder that the record was read from.

Quality flag on a numeric value, which is kept, not removed: unit_factor (the value differs from the species' other values by almost exactly x10, x100, x1000 or x25.4, the signature of a unit or per-100/per-1000-seeds slip) and/or trait_extreme (outside the 0.1-99.9 percentile of all values of the trait). Empty when neither applies. Species summaries use medians, so a flagged value barely moves them.

Identifier of this row, EB_1 .. EB_n, assigned once when the dataset is finished. One row, one id. It follows row order, so it is stable only while the dataset is not regenerated; record_id_crosswalk.csv.gz is what re-links ids to rows after a rebuild.
Number of individuals, observations or replicates behind the value, when the source states it. Needed to weight a mean and to convert a standard error to a standard deviation.
Folder holding the source dataset, as organised in this database.

What the value is: a single or unspecified value, a mean, median, minimum, maximum, standard deviation (sd), standard error (se), or a sample size (n). A value marked sd or se is a dispersion, not a measurement.

Whether the number is in the trait's standard unit: converted_or_already_target (it is), unit_missing (the source stated no unit and the value is assumed to be in the standard unit), needs_unit_check (the unit could not be resolved, so the value is as the source gave it), not_applicable (the trait has no unit).
Diaspore or dispersal-unit color name or categorical color class.
Dry mass or dry weight of the diaspore or dispersal unit.
Diaspore or dispersal-unit length.
Diaspore or dispersal-unit thickness/height; spelling follows the reviewed TRY fine-trait audit label.
Diaspore or dispersal-unit type.
Diaspore or dispersal-unit width.
Derived broad dispersal category for dispersal_mode records: biotic, abiotic, or autochorous.
Continuous seed or fruit dispersal distance.
Categorical or ordinal class describing seed or fruit dispersal distance.
Maximum seed, fruit, or diaspore dispersal distance.
Dispersal-kernel category, function, parameter, or summary descriptor.
Derived dispersal mechanism for dispersal_mode records, describing how the propagule is moved.
Derived dispersal vector for dispersal_mode records, describing the dispersing agent when identifiable.
Broad pollination mode, scored as biotic or abiotic.
Pollination syndrome, such as anemophily, entomophily, ornithophily, chiropterophily, hydrophily, autophily, or zoophily.
Pollinator group, such as bee, bird, bat, fly, lepidoptera, beetle, ant, or wasp.
Maturation age
Plant size or age at reproductive maturity.
Categorical self-compatibility state, such as self-compatible, self-incompatible, or mixed/partial.
Numeric self-compatibility, self-incompatibility, or autofertility index; paired category/context should indicate fruit set, seed set, total, or similar basis.
Plant sexual system, such as hermaphroditic, monoecious, dioecious, gynodioecious, androdioecious, or unisexual.
Fruit dehiscence category, such as dehiscent or indehiscent.
Time required for fruit development or maturation.
Fruit diameter.
Fruit dry mass or dry weight.
Fruit length.
Fruit fresh mass or fruit mass when fresh/dry basis is unspecified.
Fruit number or count; source context should indicate per plant, per infructescence, or other denominator.
Fruit lipid content expressed as a proportion or percentage.
General fruit size measurement when the dimension is not more specifically identified.
Fruit energy content per unit mass.
Total energetic content of a fruit.
Fruit type, morphology, or dryness/fleshiness class.
Fruit water content expressed as a proportion or percentage.
Fruit width.
Duration of the fruiting period.
Month in which fruiting ends, as the month name: January to December. A source that writes the month as a number or an abbreviation is converted to the name (6 and Jun both become June).
Month in which fruiting starts, as the month name: January to December. A source that writes the month as a number or an abbreviation is converted to the name (6 and Jun both become June).
Fruit color name or categorical fruit color class.
Fruit color RGB value as reported by the source.
Fruit color blue-channel value.
Fruit color brightness, lightness, value, or luminance.
Whether the fruit is conspicuous or inconspicuous as stated by the source.

Dominant wavelength of the fruit's reflectance spectrum, in nanometres (about 300-780: near-UV to far red). Separate from fruit_color_hue because a wavelength and a hue step are not interconvertible; Sinnott-Armstrong et al. 2018 report it from spectra.
Fruit color green-channel value.

Hue of the fruit colour on whatever scale the source used, which the record's unit states: munsell_hue_step for an ordinal step around the Munsell hue circle. A wavelength in nanometres is held by fruit_color_dominant_wavelength instead. The trait has no standard unit, so values on different scales must not be pooled.
Fruit color red-channel value.
Fruit color saturation or chroma-like quantitative value.
Conspicuousness of the dispersal unit (fruit or seed) as stated by the source (TRY: fruit/seed conspicuous).
Seed color name or categorical seed color class.
Seed diameter.
Seed height or thickness.
Seed length.
Seed fresh mass or seed mass when fresh/dry basis is unspecified.
Seed dry mass or dry weight.
Seed number or count; source context should indicate per fruit, per plant, or other denominator.
Seed output or seed production expressed as seeds per individual plant; source context should indicate whether this is annual, total, typical range, or another basis.
Seed width.
Corolla area.
Corolla length.
Corolla width.
Floral depth or access depth measurement.
Duration of individual flower function or opening.
Floral reward category, such as nectar, pollen, oil, resin, or no reward.
Floral symmetry category.
Flower diameter.
Flower number or count; source context should indicate per plant, per inflorescence, or other denominator.
Flower shape or floral morphology category.
General flower size measurement when the dimension is not more specifically identified.
Duration of the flowering period.
Month in which flowering ends, as the month name: January to December. A source that writes the month as a number or an abbreviation is converted to the name (6 and Jun both become June).
Month in which flowering starts, as the month name: January to December. A source that writes the month as a number or an abbreviation is converted to the name (6 and Jun both become June).
Inflorescence type or inflorescence architecture category.
Nectar sugar concentration.
Nectar volume.
Petal length.
Petal width.
Floral tube length.
Floral tube width.
Flower, corolla, or petal color name or categorical color class.
Flower ultraviolet reflectance value or score.
Flower color blue-channel value.
Whether the flower is conspicuous or inconspicuous as stated by the source.
Flower color green-channel value.
Flower color red-channel value.
Plant habit or growth form, such as tree, shrub, herb, climber/liana, palm, epiphyte, graminoid, or succulent.
Life span or life-cycle category, such as annual, biennial, perennial, or woody/herbaceous duration classes.
Plant height.
Plant longevity or maximum lifespan as a quantitative value.
Mycorrhizal association or mycorrhizal type.

Whether the fruit is dry or fleshy: as stated by the source, or given by the fruit type (capsule, legume, nut, achene, follicle, caryopsis, schizocarp, samara, silique, utricle, plumed: dry; berry, pome, syconium: fleshy).
